text:
ada: Quick follow-up on the SLA vs soft-shed tradeoffs we hashed out in the RFC meeting.
matt: TL;DR: we either guarantee per-tenant latency/SLA via reserved paths or we accept occasional soft-sheds that degrade gracefully.
zara: We shouldn't present two conflicting contracts to customers. If a tenant has an SLA, the runtime must avoid soft-shed for their traffic.
jj: Agreed, but reserved capacity is expensive. For small/medium tenants we need cheaper options that still feel reliable.
ada: Proposal: three admission tiers — Guaranteed (hard reserve), BestEffort (priority queue + burst buffer), and Probation (soft-shed + strict abuse checks).
olga: How do we signal that in the API? A single admit call with a policy flag? Or separate endpoints per tier?
matt: Keep a single admission API but return an admit_response with fields: {decision: allow/queue/deny, lease_id, expected_wait_ms, fallback_model}. Quick sketch:
```
admit(req) -> { decision: "queue", lease_id: "L-123", est_wait_ms: 150, fallback: "smol-1" }
```
zara: We need to keep surface area small for client SDKs. The SDK can expose helpers: pinned(true) -> use Guaranteed else call admit and handle queue.
jj: Abuse prevention needs to plug into this. If a tenant triggers abuse heuristics we should move them to Probation automatically and also emit a short TTL'd penalty token.
ada: Right — but important design boundary: the admission service decides routing and immediate decisions; the abuse detector is a separate service that feeds signals. Admission must be tolerant of stale signals (no hard-coupling synchronous check on path).
olga: That implies eventual consistency for penalties. Do we accept a window where a bad client keeps using cached leases before penalty applied?
matt: We do. To reduce impact we can attach a short per-lease nonce and make the runtime check a revocation list periodically. Not heavy weight but gives a fast kill switch.
jj: Ops question: revocation frequency impacts performance. If we poll every 5s it's heavy; if we poll every 60s abuse clients might get many tokens. Maybe publish revocations via pubsub so runtime gets near real-time.
ada: Pubsub + lease nonces sounds good. Also consider a soft-credit accounting model: tenants have a credit balance that drifts up slowly (recharge) and drains with usage. If below threshold, they land in Probation.
zara: Credits are nice UX for burstiness. But we must avoid inflation; recharge rate must be conservative and configurable per account.
jj: Telemetry requirements: per-admit decision type, queue time distribution, revocation events, abuse-score history. We need labels for tenant_id, route, model, admission_tier.
matt: Long-term refactor idea: decouple token accounting into a separate ledger service with strong append-only semantics. Admission queries that ledger for instantaneous balance and receives leases. This would let us reason about cross-region consistency later.
olga: Ledger service adds complexity but gives cleaner ownership and easier audits (compliance loves append-only ledgers).
ada: Rollout plan: feature-flag admit API changes behind a canary. Start with non-critical routes (embeddings) -> monitor queue times and increase canary if 1) 99p queue < 200ms and 2) no revocations spike.
sre-bot: deploy-canary: admission-v2 flagged on prod-noncritical at 2026-03-29T03:00Z :eyes:
zara: For the RFC follow-up, we need an action list: 1) finalize admit_response schema (matt) 2) design revocation pubsub topic & runtime handshake (jj) 3) credit model param proposal (zara) 4) ledger feasibility doc (olga) 5) telemetry dashboard template (ada)
matt: I'll push admit_response proto tomorrow and add a short backwards-compatible compat layer.
jj: I'll prototype revocation pubsub with lambda consumer and benchmark an end-to-end revoke-to-drop latency.
olga: I'll write a short ledger feasibility note (consensus, recovery, cost) by next Wed.
zara: I'll draft credit recharge math and some sample configs for Bronze/Silver/Gold accounts.
ada: Awesome. If nobody objects, I'll post this as the official follow-up and set up a 30m check-in next Tue.
matt: :thumbsup:
jj: +1
olga: +1
